Subject: Embed stabilization roadmap + rerank canary matrix — kickoff

Emma / team —

Thanks for the time on Tuesday. Per our conversation, I wanted to put a short, actionable kickoff note that pulls together the implementation checkpoints we discussed and a proposed canary/eval approach for reranking. The goal here is to give Nova Product a low-risk, incremental path to move embeddings + rerank into production while keeping query latency predictable.

High level objectives
- Seed/backfill strategy that avoids large cold-start latency spikes
- Clear DB compatibility guardrails (vector similarity parity, metadata filters, ttl)
- Rerank evaluation matrix to detect regressions early (NDCG, answer correctness, latency delta)

Proposed three-phase plan (draft)
1) Warmstart (wave 0) — small seed (~50k vectors) for live traffic reroutes; validate priming and KV cache behavior
2) Backfill waves — staged backfill by content type (docs, Q&A, help-center) with throttled write rates and health checks
3) Canary and cutover — A/B rerank test across 5% / 50% traffic buckets, safety fallback to baseline model

Vector DB considerations (tradeoffs we need to decide up front)
- Managed vs self-hosted: latency SLAs vs egress + access patterns
- Filtering & metadata match semantics (important for your category filters)
- Snapshot / index versioning to support rollback and partial reindexing
- Cost model: cold vs hot memory requirements for dense vectors

Rerank eval plan (short)
- Metrics: NDCG@5, MRR, latency 95th/99th, regressions flagged if NDCG drops > 2% or latency 95th increases > 40ms
- Datasets: use the priming_samples.csv (attached) + we’ll add 500 check queries from your production logs
- Acceptance gates: pass on two consecutive daily smoke runs for 72 hours

Immediate asks from Nova Product
1) Sample export of 10k queries + expected relevance (or signal we can use as proxy)
2) Vector DB preference (Pinecone / Milvus / Weaviate / internal) and whether you have a license for self-hosting
3) Confirm timezone for weekly status (we proposed Tuesdays 9am PST)

Attachments: redwood-embed-migration-runbook.pdf (ops runbook), priming_samples.csv, rerank-eval-template.xlsx

I'll compile a mutual action plan after we get the sample data. Proposed owners: Mateo (tech lead), Marissa (CSM / MAP), Soojin (onboarding QA & evals).

Thanks —
Mateo

Hey all — quick technical notes from our side:

- We prefer Milvus for cost and existing infra. We'll provision a staging cluster (v2.2) for the warmstart. We can give a read-only user for seeding and smoke tests.
- Index versioning: we have a snapshot process that tags indexes; we'll expose snapshot IDs but we need your runtime to accept a snapshot ID on startup so we can rollback quickly if needed.
- Priming concerns: cold KV filling is expected; we want to measure token-level latency impact during the warmstart and limit concurrent priming to 100 requests/sec to avoid cache stomping.

Also — can you confirm how Redwood handles partial index merges? Our dataset has several doc types and we may only want to reindex new docs initially.

Thanks,
Sam Torres
Senior Platform Engineer, Nova Product

All —

Thanks for the clarifications and the quick turn on samples. Based on the thread above, here’s a finalized, short owner-level plan and immediate next steps:

Phase 0 — Warmstart (owner: Sam / Mateo)
- Deliverable: seed 50k vectors to staging Milvus cluster (snapshot-enabled) by 2026-11-30
- Smoke tests: 24hr run validating NDCG baseline + latency 95th; throttles at 100 rps for priming

Phase 1 — Backfill waves (owner: Marissa / Sam)
- Wave 1 (docs): staged backfill week of 2026-12-06 with throttled writes; health checks every 2 hours
- Safety: automatic fallback route to baseline search tier if 502s cross 1% or latency 95th degrades > 40ms

Phase 2 — Canary & Cutover (owner: Mateo / Soojin)
- Canary ramp: 5% → 20% → 50% over three healthy gates (24hr each)
- Acceptance: two consecutive daily smoke runs with NDCG change within ±2% and P95 latency within threshold

Action items (this week)
- Nova: upload sample export + 1k labeled subset (Lina) — due Wed 11/25 (received)
- Sam: provision staging Milvus + read-only seed account — due Mon 11/29
- Marissa: publish MAP in HubSpot and create recurring Tuesday cadence — due Mon 11/29
- Mateo / Soojin: prepare rerank eval jobs and dashboard (P95, NDCG) — due Tue 12/01

Notes on partial merges & index versioning
- We’ll support seeding by snapshot ID and incremental document add (no full rebuild required). For large-scale merges we recommend doing a phased reindex per doc-type to limit blast radius.

Links: MAP draft is on HubSpot (see link above) and runbook attached for ops playbook.

If there are no blockers I’ll schedule the warmstart checkpoint for Tue 11/30 9am PST — please accept the calendar invite when you get it.

Thanks —
